chunks: From al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

A man dies and there are no others with him except women. He said: “His wife washes him, because she is still of him during the waiting period ('iddah). But if she dies, he does not wash her, because he is not of her during a waiting period.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning of his statement عليه السلام, “and if she dies, he does not wash her,” is that he does not wash her stripped of her clothes; rather, he washes her from behind the garment. That is indicated by what he has narrated:

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: she performs the ritual washing of the deceased upon him
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period, used here as the legal basis mentioned in the narration
key_terms.لَمْ يُغَسِّلْهَا: he does not wash her, as stated in the outward wording of the report
key_terms.مُجَرَّدَةً: stripped or unclothed, clarifying the restricted meaning
key_terms.مِنْ وَرَاءِ ٱلثَّوْبِ: from behind the garment, indicating the manner of washing
key_terms.ٱمْرَأَتُهُ: his wife, the spouse discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife perform ghusl for their deceased spouse in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning the washing of the deceased between spouses. It states that a wife may wash her deceased husband, and Shaykh al-Tusi explains that the husband's washing of his deceased wife is understood as being done from behind a garment, not with her unclothed.
